newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs firmer on short-covering, buying on dips.
newsitem.headline: JGBs firmer on short-covering, buying on dips.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract was firmer by midday on Friday, due to short-covering and buying of cash bonds on dips.
"Long-liquidation and hedge selling took the September down initially, but buying on dips later set in and triggered short-covering," a trader for a foreign brokerage house said.
Traders said the September fell to a morning low of 126.30 in early trade, as the key futures contract tried to fill a gap on technical charts between 126.28 and 126.32.
The September stood at 126.47 by midday, up slightly from the previous day's close of 126.45. Turnover was 11,455 lots.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.120 percent as of 0226 GMT, up slightly from Thursday's close of 2.110 percent.
Traders said the market would be watching Japan July domestic vehicle sales data due at 2 p.m. (0500 GMT).
But they said activity was likely to be quiet ahead of the weekend and the release of key U.S. jobs data.
"It will probably be difficult for traders to build outright positions as U.S. jobs data is coming up," the trader for a foreign brokerage house said.
The Finance Ministry's Trust Fund Bureau offered to buy 100 billion yen in bonds outright in an agreement starting on August 6, the Bank of Japan said on Friday.
There was little effect from MOF's outright bond buying, traders said.

JGBs fell on LIFFE overnight due to a comment by Keidanren chairman Shoichiro Toyoda on Thursday that the Japanese economy appears to be improving and that it may be time to raise the official discount rate, traders said.
But the impact from the comment was limited, as it was considered a rehashing of previous remarks, they said.
